the risk of radiation-induced neoplasms after stereotactic radiosurgery.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stereotactic radiation may cause a sarcoma in a young patient with a neurofibromatotic predisposition.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stereotactic radiation treatment of vestibular schwannomata may cause a mesenchymal tumor at the site of irradiation.
the development of a sarcoma in a NF-2 patient after SRT should be considered as a possible complication.
the development of mesenchymal neoplasms after SRT is not a rare event.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SRT may cause malignant transformation.
the risk of developing a postirradiation tumor should be discussed with all patients who are candidates for stereotactic radiosurgery.
SRT should not be used for the treatment of vestibular schwannomata in patients with neurofibromatoses.
